productionReasons.s0030/en: Restore Liaodong, the target of the personal campaign (自征遼東).
productionReasons.s0031/en: Restore the office 令 and render 居就 as Jujiu in both English fields and repeated uses.
productionReasons.s0031/literal: Correct the paired-field Juqiu reading; retain the existing explicit magistrate office.
productionReasons.s0060/en: Restore repeated border trouble, the general title and the specific request for troops; name Huang explicitly to avoid attributing his vassalage to the envoy.
productionReasons.s0060/literal: The source explicitly makes Huang (皝) the subject, but the existing literal English has no subject before sent. Restore the explicit subject while preserving the general title, repeated frontier trouble, vassalage and troop request.
productionReasons.s0065/en: Render 旬餘 as more than ten days, 左右 as attendants, and make Huang the explicit recipient of their advice.
productionReasons.s0082/en: Restore the omitted 建威 title and the long-established fame and prestige; preserve the complete account of feigned madness.
productionReasons.s0082/literal: Translate 建威 as an office, rather than leaving Jianwei as an apparent personal name; retain all paired-field propositions.
productionReasons.s0084/en: Restore 陰 and the explicit observation target; render 撫膺 without changing it to clutching.
productionReasons.s0091/en: Proposed passive rendering preserves the unexpressed Chinese subject without silently choosing Huang as grantor. This does not resolve the held extraction event attribution.
productionReasons.s0091/literal: Preserve the enfeoffment and number without supplying an unexpressed grantor; independently review in the complete imperial-grant context.
productionReasons.s0168/en: Explicitly mark the Tongjian variant behind loath to kill you, retain the opposite extant Jinshu reading and Jinshu Jiaozhu judgment, and point to the full literal note. Preserve the Chinese source and all textual uncertainty; this resolves the independently identified unmarked emendation.
productionReasons.s0168/literal: Preserve the extant literal reading and append the independently reviewed philological note documenting the divergent Tongjian and Yulan witnesses. The Chinese source itself remains unchanged.
productionReasons.s0179/en: Restore the unexpected failure of his resolve, his lingering regret at death and the final rhetorical question; preserve the closing quotation.
productionReasons.s0183/en: 雖宗族無能識者 means none of the clan recognized his worth, not merely that few knew him; 幼 refers to Yu when Dan recognized his promise.
productionReasons.s0183/literal: Paired-field source review: preserve every proposition while correcting the same mistaken reading or omission as the idiomatic proposal. productionReasons.s0193/en: Correct the Mencius quotation: Yi Yin may serve any ruler and command any people; 使 does not mean serving the people. Preserve the bottle-gourd example, sages and worthies, and complete surrounding speech.

productionReasons.s0214/literal: In 皆豫其謀, 豫 stands for 與 and means to take part in. Yu took part in the planning of both campaigns. 'Pre-planned their strategies' misreads 豫 as 'beforehand'. The idiomatic field already says 'He helped plan' correctly, so only that clause in the literal field changes.

candidateDecisions.note: The Chinese 自征遼東 names Liaodong as the place targeted by Huang’s campaign, not an individual. The independently approved English restores this explicit geographical object.

Jinshu Jiaozhu is the cited critical annotation work, corresponding to the independently reviewed 晉書斠注 reference. Its English title occurs only in the explicit textual-variant note and does not identify a person.

proofSupersessions.reason: The original approved literal keeps the extant reading and a philological note. The separately reviewed successor renders the same note and witnesses entirely in English because the production editorial gate rejects Chinese in reviewed English replacements. No Chinese source or historical proposition changes; the original approval remains immutable provenance.

The original approved idiomatic wording used the Tongjian variant without marking it, as independently found by the first application reviewer. The independently approved successor explicitly marks that basis, preserves the opposite extant Jinshu reading and the critical judgment, and points to the complete literal note. Original source and earlier reports remain unchanged.
